newsitem.title: USA: CHICAGO FED SEES NO LOCAL WAGE PRESSURE ON PRICES.
newsitem.headline: CHICAGO FED SEES NO LOCAL WAGE PRESSURE ON PRICES.

text.p: Wages have gone up somewhat in the seventh U.S. economic district, but the phenomenon has not yet put any upward pressure on local retail prices, said an economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago.
"We get some reports of there being some wage pressures, but nothing too extreme," William Strauss, economist at the Chicago Fed told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
"We're still not seeing any kind of pressure being built up on the wage side," the economist added.
Strauss spoke to RFTV shortly after the Chicago Fed announced its midwest manufacturing index was down 0.1 percent in June against a revised 0.4 drop in May.
The index gauges industrial activity in the seventh U.S. economic district, which includes Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Michigan, and Wisconsin.
